content.title: About
content.content: Candy Mint (5111) are small mint-flavored candies coated with a sugary glaze. They offer a refreshing mint taste combined with a sweet note, making them a popular treat after meals and as a breath freshener.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Candy Mint first appeared in the early 20th century in Europe as a breath‑freshening confection.
The sugary glaze helps preserve the mint aroma longer.
The recipe often includes natural menthol, which intensifies the cooling sensation.
These candies are frequently used in film and theater as a prop for “minty” scenes.
In some countries they are sold in small packets of 10–20 pieces.

items.title: Freshens breath
items.content: Menthol and mint stimulate saliva production, neutralizing unpleasant mouth odors.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Mint can help ease mild gastrointestinal discomfort.

items.title: Reduces fatigue
items.content: The menthol aroma provides a mild stimulating effect, increasing alertness.

items.title: Menthol allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to menthol or flavoring agents.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption can contribute to tooth decay and raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Large amounts of mint candies may cause heartburn in people with high gastric acidity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Candy Mint is best enjoyed one at a time, allowing the menthol to gradually release its aroma. They can be taken after a meal, as a small snack, or added to dessert presentations for a minty accent.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the candies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Properly stored, they retain flavor and aroma for up to 12 months.

nutritional-drink-or-shake-ready-to-drin.title: Nutritional drink or shake, ready-to-drink, NFS

content.title: About
content.content: NFS nutritional drink is a ready‑to‑drink shake that provides a balanced blend of proteins, carbohydrates, fats, vitamins, and minerals. It is designed to support energy, post‑workout recovery, and convenient nutrition throughout the day.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: NFS is produced using cold‑press technology, preserving the bioactivity of its ingredients.
It contains plant proteins such as pea and soy, as well as whey protein.
Each serving delivers over 20 g of protein and up to 30 % of the daily value of vitamin D.
The product is free from artificial colors and flavors.
Packaging is made from recyclable aluminum, reducing environmental impact.

items.title: Supports muscle recovery
items.content: High‑quality fast‑digesting protein helps repair muscle fibers after physical activity.

items.title: Provides an energy boost
items.content: A balanced carbohydrate profile supplies steady energy without sharp blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Vitamin‑mineral complex
items.content: Includes B‑vitamins, vitamin C, iron, and calcium to support immunity and bone health.

items.title: Convenient consumption
items.content: Ready‑to‑drink format requires no preparation, ideal for travel and work.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Contains prebiotic fibers that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Milk or soy protein allergy
items.content: The drink contains milk and soy proteins, which may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Added sugar in some flavors
items.content: Certain variants contain added sugars; people monitoring glucose should choose unsweetened options.

items.title: Caloric content
items.content: One serving provides about 250 kcal, so it should be accounted for in total daily intake when managing weight.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Some flavors are fortified with caffeine; caffeine‑sensitive individuals should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink directly from the bottle or chill before consumption. For extra flavor, add ice, fruit, or herbs. The recommended serving is 300 ml per day, but up to two servings can be taken for higher energy needs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5 days. Discard the product after the expiration date printed on the packaging.

content.title: About
content.content: Pickles, sweet are fresh cucumbers that have been brined in a sweet solution containing sugar, vinegar, spices, and sometimes aromatic herbs. They have a crisp texture, a sweet‑sour flavor, and a bright aroma, making them a popular addition to snacks, salads, and sandwiches.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet pickling recipes originated in Eastern Europe in the 19th century as a way to preserve cucumbers.
Traditional blends often include cinnamon, cloves, and allspice, giving a distinctive aroma.
Sweet pickles are commonly used in cold appetizers and festive salads.
They can be found whole, sliced into rings, or cut into spears.
In some countries they are served with mustard or horseradish to enhance flavor.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Sweet pickles contain virtually no fat, making them a light snack.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Cucumbers provide a good amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber in pickles aids normal digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: One cup of sweet pickles contains about 30 kcal, suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sweet brines can contain significant amounts of sugar, which may be unsuitable for people with diabetes or those limiting sugar intake.

items.title: Vinegar acidity
items.content: Vinegar may irritate the stomach in individuals with high acidity or gastritis.

items.title: Salt in the brine
items.content: Excessive salt intake can contribute to elevated blood pressure.

items.title: Spice allergies
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to spices used in the brine, such as mustard or coriander.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sweet pickles can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to salads, sandwiches, rolls, or used as a garnish for meat dishes. They are often served alongside cheese, cold cuts, or smoked foods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the jar of sweet pickles in the refrigerator at 2 °C–5 °C. Once opened, consume within 2–3 weeks. Discard if mold, off‑odors, or discoloration appear.

pretzels-soft-ready-to-eat-coated-or-fla.title: Soft Pretzels, Ready‑to‑Eat, Coated or Flavored

content.title: About
content.content: Soft pretzels are a ready‑to‑eat baked product made from a yeasted dough that remains tender and springy after baking. They can be coated with salt, cheese, spices or sweet glazes, and flavored with a variety of tastes such as garlic, onion, paprika or caramel.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soft pretzels originated in medieval Europe as the “pretzel,” a symbol of crossed monk’s arms.
The classic shape is formed by twisting the dough into a figure‑eight, representing infinity and good luck.
In the United States, soft pretzels gained popularity in the early 1920s thanks to German immigrants.
There are more than 30 coating and flavor variations, from classic salt to chocolate and berry glazes.
Soft pretzels are a staple in fast‑food venues, movie theaters, and sporting events.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Soft pretzels provide quickly digestible carbs that can rapidly replenish energy after physical activity.

items.title: Contains modest protein
items.content: The wheat‑based dough supplies a small amount of plant‑based protein.

items.title: B‑vitamin content
items.content: Fermentation by yeast generates B1, B2 and B3 vitamins that support metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Depending on added toppings, pretzels may contribute iron, magnesium and zinc.

items.title: Psychological comfort
items.content: Warm soft pretzels are often associated with coziness and can improve mood.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Many varieties are heavily salted, which may be unsuitable for hypertension or kidney issues.

items.title: Added sugars in sweet versions
items.content: Glazes and flavorings often contain added sugar, increasing calorie density.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat flour dough contains gluten, making the product unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Soft pretzels are relatively calorie‑rich; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels can be enjoyed warm straight from the oven, sliced and spread with cream cheese, hummus, or dip. They are often served with mustard, cheese sauce, or sweet dips. Sweet‑coated pretzels make a convenient dessert or snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store soft pretzels in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator—they stay soft for up to a week. Reheat briefly in a microwave or oven before serving to restore aroma.
